5  JUDGMENT

Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 07.11.2012 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Fast Track Court-I/II, Bijapur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC Nos.1543, 1542 and 1544 of 2009, these appeals are filed.
2. Sri Sanganabasava B. Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeals were by owner of insured vehicle challenging dismissal of claim petitions against respondent no.3-insurer.

Though appeals were filed on ground that appellant herein was previous owner of insured vehicle and that owner of vehicle as on date of accident was respondent no.2 herein, said contention is not pressed,
since other ground for dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.3-insurer was that, driver of insured vehicle namely passenger auto rickshaw was a NC: 2023:KHC-K:6520 commercial cab and driver was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle without transport endorsement.
In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Mukund Dewangan v/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663, insurer cannot escape liability on this ground.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan v/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, appeals require to be allowed holding respondent no.3 liable to pay compensation.
It was submitted that if awards were modified to said extent, other grounds would not be pressed.
3. Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel for respondent no.1-claimant would sail with appellant.

4. Sri S.S. Aspalli, learned counel for respondent no.3-insurer is not able to state legal position availing after decision in Mukund Dewangan's case (supra).
5.
Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and awards and also records.
On perusal of impugned judgment, it is seen that insured vehicle involved in accident is an auto rickshaw which would be light commercial vehicle.

Ex.R3 produced by insurer before Tribunal would indicate that driver of insured vehicle had driving licence to drive light motor vehicle and validity of said licence was from 08.08.2006 to 07.08.2026.
It is not in dispute that accident herein occurred on 17.04.2009.
Therefore, said licence would be valid as on date of accident.

7. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan's case (supra) has held that, person holding licence to drive light motor vehicle would be authorised to drive any motor vehicle of gross vehicle weight less than 7500 kgs.
Since insured vehicle in question meets such description, insurer cannot escape liability.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeals are allowed.
Impugned awards are modified to extent of dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.3 and held respondent no.3-insurer liable to pay compensation.

v. In MVC no.1544/2009, it is seen that out of total award of Rs.2,76,000/-,
Rs.1,50,000/- is medical expenses, which is substantial portion of award.
It is also seen that claimant therein was 34 years of age, who sustained fracture of ribs.

Hence,
entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of claimant.
